rationale: A is better structured and more robust: it centralizes all matching semantics, including inversion, in one helper and streams files line by line. Crucially, its `-l` behavior correctly respects `-v`, whereas B’s separate filename-only branch ignores inversion and therefore mishandles combined `-l -v` usage. A has minor inefficiencies—continuing to scan after listing a file and using a redundant `listed` set—but these are less significant than B’s semantic defect and less precise naming.
